hero.lead: A nation of 53.4 million on two oceans, more than half of it forest, whose essential health care scores 82 out of 100 and whose first metro line is rising over Bogota.

capital.heading: Colombia arranges its finance before the shock arrives. Next, a safe toilet in every home.

record.text: Bogota Metro Line 1: Viaduct, stations and 23 trains
Disaster risk credit line (Cat DDO), additional financing: Budget support after the 10 August earthquake

register.name: Global bonds, three new lines
register.detail: Issued October 2026 · 5 years at 7.000% · 10 years at 7.625% · 30 years at 8.125%
register.text: Three new dollar bonds of five, ten and thirty years that finance the 2026 national budget, the Ministry of Finance said. Larger than January’s $4.95 billion sale.
by: Ministry of Finance and Public Credit of Colombia

register.name: Global bonds 2029, 2031 and 2033
register.note: Orders of about $23.2 billion from more than 290 investors
register.text: Three dollar bonds, $2.0 billion, $1.475 billion and $1.475 billion, at an average coupon of 5.93%. They covered much of the Government’s financing need for 2026.
by: Ministry of Finance and Public Credit of Colombia

register.name: Bogota international green bond
register.detail: Announced 27 November 2025 · COP 2.3 trillion · IFC and CAF as anchor investors
register.note: The city’s first international green bond
register.text: Finances the Bogota Metro, the San Cristobal and Potosi cable cars and the new Calle 13 TransMilenio corridor. Demand reached COP 3.1 trillion, 93.4% of it from international investors.

register.name: Disaster risk credit line (Cat DDO), additional financing
register.note: Budget support after the 10 August earthquake
register.text: Adds to the contingent line arranged in February 2025, so help reaches communities fast.

register.name: Bogota Metro Line 1
register.text: Funds the heaviest construction phase ahead of opening in 2028.

register.name: Multipurpose Cadaster expansion
register.note: Land records, paid on verified results
register.text: Extends the national cadaster and modernises geospatial data, so that land records serve planning, risk management and property tax, and owners can exercise their land rights. Women and vulnerable communities are trained for cadaster work.

register.name: Equitable and sustainable development reform program
register.detail: Approved 20 February 2025 · IBRD loan · Second of a series of two
register.text: Supports better targeting of social programmes, lower fossil fuel subsidies, access to credit and services for vulnerable groups, and the protection of strategic ecosystems and clean energy.

register.name: CAF approvals for five projects
register.detail: Announced 2 October 2026 · Five loans and credit lines
register.note: National and city projects, with Medellin
register.text: Up to $300 million for the Metro de Medellin, $250 million for Medellin’s development plan, a $150 million contingent credit line for reconstruction after the earthquake, $200 million for the La Dorada–Chiriguana rail corridor under a public-private partnership, and $350 million for the blue economy, biodiversity and sustainable finance.

register.name: CAF approvals for Colombia’s sustainable development
register.detail: Approved June 2025 · Climate action $350m · Mental health $150m · Aerocivil $240m
register.note: Three credit agreements signed, $740 million of the total
register.text: Approved by CAF’s board of directors: support for climate action, sustainability and biodiversity, wider access to mental health services, and the investment plan of the civil aviation authority.

register.name: Banco de Bogota financing package
register.detail: Announced 26 May 2026 · About 50% sustainable construction · 30% SMEs · 20% transition finance
register.text: Lends for certified green buildings that use less water and energy, for small firms that create jobs, and for upgrades that cut emissions, with a UK-backed green construction incentive.

register.name: Habi structured line of credit
register.detail: Announced 3 March 2026 · Two tranches of up to $25 million · Colombian pesos
register.note: Up to $50 million, housing for low and middle incomes
register.text: Finances the purchase and management of homes on Habi’s platform for low- and middle-income families, and an alternative credit score for a new mortgage line for women, young people and others with little access to credit.

register.name: Buga–Loboguerrero–Buenaventura road, sustainability-linked loan
register.detail: Signed 11 August 2025 · Colombian pesos · Part of a package of about $904 million
register.note: Terms tied to lower emissions and more women in the workforce
register.text: Improves and maintains the road from the interior to Buenaventura, the nation’s largest port, which carries 44% of its trade. A concession awarded to SACYR in 2022.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 79 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street in Medellin, Colombia

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Coffee farms on the steep green slopes of the Colombian coffee region

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Amazon rainforest in southern Colombia, river through the canopy

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A waterfall in the Colombian Andes

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: A hydropower reservoir in the mountains of Antioquia, Colombia

items.name: Habi
items.text: A proptech company founded in 2019 that buys and sells homes for low- and middle-income families through a data-driven platform, to make the market for existing homes work better.

items.name: Banco Mundo Mujer
items.text: The nation’s largest privately owned microfinance lender, serving mostly informal microentrepreneurs; about 60% of them are women.

coverage.gap_text: Colombians without a safely managed toilet at home: 81 in every hundred.
